title: The Sunday Read: 'The Movement to Bring Death Closer'

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》每日简讯《DealBook》的商业与政策记者。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 在11月18日，我将在纽约市的DealBook峰会上现场采访商界、政界和文化界最具影响力的领袖，包括万斯、

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde,
sentences.zh: 埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、

sentences.en: Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的真实对话。

sentences.zh: 我希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Hi, my name is Maggie Jones.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我叫玛吉·琼斯。

sentences.en: I'm a contributing writer for The New York Times Magazine, and I teach writing at the University of Pittsburgh.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报杂志》的特约撰稿人，并在匹兹堡大学教授写作。

sentences.en: I wrote a story about a year ago about a group of people who call themselves home funeral guides, and their mission is to help us be less afraid and more in touch with death.
sentences.zh: 大约一年前，我写过一篇报道，关于一群自称为“居家葬礼指导”的人，他们的使命是帮助我们减少对死亡的恐惧，并更多地去面对死亡。

sentences.en: You might think that the story about home funerals is incredibly depressing, and I get that.
sentences.zh: 你可能会觉得关于居家葬礼的故事极其压抑，我理解这种感受。

sentences.en: It's a story about death and loss.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于死亡和失落的故事。

sentences.en: But in the course of my reporting about it, I actually found this process to be incredibly life-affirming and even beautiful.
sentences.zh: 但在我的报道过程中，我实际上发现这个过程非常肯定生命，甚至很美妙。

sentences.en: Usually in this country, as soon as somebody dies, the ambulance or the funeral home comes almost right away.
sentences.zh: 通常在这个国家，一旦有人去世，救护车或殡仪馆几乎马上就会来。

sentences.en: It can be within minutes.
sentences.zh: 可能就在几分钟之内。

sentences.en: And that may be the last time you see the body.
sentences.zh: 那可能是你最后一次见到这具遗体。

sentences.en: It gets whisked away, and that's it.
sentences.zh: 它会被迅速带走，然后就结束了。

sentences.en: But in the home funeral movement, the idea is instead that after your loved one dies, you might spend several hours with them, or you might spend up to three days.
sentences.zh: 但在居家葬礼运动中，其理念反而是：在你爱的人去世后，你可能会和他们共处几个小时，或者长达三天。

sentences.en: The home funeral guides are there to let the families have as much control over the process as they want.
sentences.zh: 居家葬礼指导的存在是为了让家属尽可能多地掌控这个过程。

sentences.en: That may mean that they want to dress and bathe the body, comb their hair.
sentences.zh: 这可能意味着他们想要为遗体穿衣、洗澡、梳头。

sentences.en: They may want to put lots of flowers around the room and play music and light candles.
sentences.zh: 他们可能想在房间里摆上许多鲜花、播放音乐、点燃蜡烛。

sentences.en: And the key is it's what the family wants.
sentences.zh: 关键在于，这是家属想要的。

sentences.en: Death is, you know, it's out of our control.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，死亡是超出我们控制的。

sentences.en: There's nothing we can do.
sentences.zh: 我们无能为力。

sentences.en: We don't get to decide when loved ones die, when we die.
sentences.zh: 我们无法决定爱的人什么时候死，我们什么时候死。

sentences.en: But the power of this movement is that it returns a bit of that control to families.
sentences.zh: 但这场运动的力量在于，它将一部分控制权交还给了家属。

sentences.en: And that can be profoundly comforting.
sentences.zh: 这可以带来极大的安慰。

sentences.en: I think for me, the message is that we don't have to rush death.
sentences.zh: 对我而言，这个信息是：我们不必急于处理死亡。

sentences.en: And in fact, sitting with it can make the process a little easier.
sentences.zh: 事实上，静静陪伴可能会让这个过程变得稍微轻松一些。

sentences.en: So here's my story, The Movement to Bring Death Closer, read by January Lavoie.
sentences.zh: 以下是我的报道《让死亡更近的运动》，由简·拉武瓦朗读。

sentences.en: Heidi Boucher loaded two big straw baskets into her Toyota Highlander.
sentences.zh: 海蒂·布歇把两个大草篮装进了她的丰田汉兰达里。

sentences.en: She always kept them packed, ready for death.
sentences.zh: 她总是把它们收拾好，为死亡做好准备。

sentences.en: Inside were a pair of leather work gloves and a hammer, a bunch of bed pads, a few adult diapers, dead bodies sometimes leak,
sentences.zh: 里面有一副皮质工作手套和一个锤子、一堆床垫、几条成人纸尿裤（遗体有时会渗液）、

sentences.en: Q-tips for cleaning ears, noses, and mouths, and for applying lipstick, cotton balls, disinfectant spray,
sentences.zh: 用于清洁耳朵、鼻子、嘴巴以及涂抹口红的棉签、棉球、消毒喷雾、

sentences.en: a plastic zip bag of safety pins to help drape silk and other fabrics around a gurney or casket, a small screwdriver to tightly close a casket, latex gloves, a hairbrush,
sentences.zh: 装着安全别针的塑料拉链袋（用来将丝绸和其他织物披在推车或棺材上）、一把用来紧紧关上棺材的小螺丝刀、乳胶手套、一把发刷，

sentences.en: and oils infused with rose, lavender, and rosemary.
sentences.zh: 以及注入了玫瑰、薰衣草和迷迭香精油的精油。

sentences.en: Boucher also had her black attache case of paperwork on funeral planning, which included a few funeral home price lists for cremation and other services,
sentences.zh: 布歇还有一个装着殡葬规划文件的黑色公文包，里面包括几份关于火化和其他服务的殡仪馆价格表，

sentences.en: as well as the files of 20 or so clients who had already made plans for Boucher to help with their bodies after death.
sentences.zh: 以及大约20位客户的档案，这些客户已经做好了安排，希望布歇在他们死后协助处理他们的遗体。

sentences.en: Among them was Susan Lerure, a 79-year-old wife, mother, grandmother, reading teacher at a community college, lover of nature, spontaneity, and books.
sentences.zh: 其中有79岁的苏珊·勒尔尔，她是一位妻子、母亲、祖母，社区大学的阅读老师，也是大自然、随性和书籍的爱好者。

sentences.en: Lerure had died about an hour earlier in her home in Oakland, California, and Boucher was on her way to her.
sentences.zh: 勒尔尔大约一小时前在她位于加利福尼亚州奥克兰的家中去世，布歇正赶往她那里。

sentences.en: Over the last few decades,
sentences.zh: 在过去几十年里，

sentences.en: Boucher has helped more than 100 families take care of loved ones' bodies in the hours and days after death.
sentences.zh: 布歇已经帮助了100多位家属在亲人去世后的数小时和数天内照料遗体。

sentences.en: Some of their deaths were long expected, whether from cancer, multiple sclerosis, or another chronic disease.
sentences.zh: 他们有些人的死亡是预料之中的，无论是死于癌症、多发性硬化症还是其他慢性疾病。

sentences.en: But she also helps families with the sudden, inconceivable loss.
sentences.zh: 但她也帮助那些遭遇突然、难以想象之痛的家属。

sentences.en: The teenager who jumped from the Golden Gate Bridge.
sentences.zh: 从金门大桥跳下的青少年。

sentences.en: The man who shot himself.
sentences.zh: 开枪自杀的男子。

sentences.en: The children and adults killed in car and motorcycle accidents.
sentences.zh: 在汽车和摩托车事故中丧生的儿童和成年人。

sentences.en: The people who died of drug overdoses.
sentences.zh: 死于药物过量的人。

sentences.en: They have been atheists, Christians, Buddhists, Jews.
sentences.zh: 他们中有无神论者、基督徒、佛教徒、犹太人。

sentences.en: Boucher, who describes herself as a home death care guide, is in her mid-fifties, with an earthy, hip style.
sentences.zh: 自称为居家临终关怀指导的布歇五十多岁，有着朴实、前卫的风格。

sentences.en: Dark hair piled loosely atop her head.
sentences.zh: 深色头发松松地盘在头顶。

sentences.en: A stack of gold bangles on her left wriSt.
sentences.zh: 左手腕上戴着一叠金色手镯。

sentences.en: Silver hoop earrings.
sentences.zh: 银色大耳环。

sentences.en: Chunky black glasses.
sentences.zh: 粗框黑眼镜。

sentences.en: The oldest daughter of five, and a mother of three adult children, she has a maternal warmth and deep-set blue eyes that draw people to share their confidences.
sentences.zh: 作为五个孩子中的老大和三个成年孩子的母亲，她有着母性的温暖和深邃的蓝眼睛，吸引着人们向她吐露心声。

sentences.en: For the grieving,
sentences.zh: 对于悲伤的人来说，

sentences.en: Boucher likens death care to walking into a pool, to avoid the shock of jumping into the cold.
sentences.zh: 布歇将临终关怀比作走进泳池，以避免跳进冷水中的休克。

sentences.en: Some people like jumping into the cold.
sentences.zh: 有些人喜欢跳进冷水里。

sentences.en: But virtually everyone who has had a conventional funeral and later comes to me, says that they wish they had more time.
sentences.zh: 但几乎所有举办过传统葬礼后来找我的人都说，他们希望当时能有更多时间。

sentences.en: Susan Lerure wanted her children and husband to have time.
sentences.zh: 苏珊·勒尔尔希望她的孩子和丈夫能有时间。

sentences.en: She had been living with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis,
sentences.zh: 她患有肌萎缩侧索硬化症，

sentences.en: ALS, for a few years.
sentences.zh: 也就是渐冻症，已经好几年了。

sentences.en: Her legs stopped working.
sentences.zh: 她的双腿停止了工作。

sentences.en: Next, her arMs.
sentences.zh: 接着是她的手臂。

sentences.en: Then her breathing became more difficult, and she had trouble swallowing.
sentences.zh: 然后她的呼吸变得更加困难，吞咽也出现了问题。

sentences.en: She knew she wanted to be cremated.
sentences.zh: 她知道自己想要火化。

sentences.en: And though she typically had strong opinions, she left the funeral details up to her family.
sentences.zh: 尽管她通常很有主见，但她把葬礼的细节留给了家人。

sentences.en: When we talked late last year,
sentences.zh: 当我们在去年年底交谈时，

sentences.en: Susan was in her bedroom overlooking a golf course and a group of trees, including her favorite redwood.
sentences.zh: 苏珊正待在她的卧室里，窗外俯瞰着一个高尔夫球场和一片树林，其中包括她最喜欢的红木。

sentences.en: I'm glad I'm not going to be whisked away and waxed up in a funeral home, she said.
sentences.zh: 她曾说：“我很高兴我不会被迅速带走并在殡仪馆里涂上防腐蜡。”

sentences.en: Her daughter, Suzanne, an art history teacher and a gallery owner, had heard about Boucher from someone at her daughter's school.
sentences.zh: 她的女儿苏珊娜是一名艺术史老师兼画廊老板，从她女儿学校的人那里听说了布歇。

sentences.en: She had also watched a documentary on home funerals called In the Parlor,
sentences.zh: 她还看过一部名为《在客厅里：

sentences.en: The Final Goodbye, written, directed, and produced by Boucher.
sentences.zh: 最后的告别》的关于居家葬礼的纪录片，该片由布歇编剧、导演和制作。

sentences.en: Boucher, who lives in Fair Oaks, California, is also an independent TV and film and production designer.
sentences.zh: 住在加利福尼亚州费尔奥克斯的布歇，同时也是一位独立的电视、电影和制作设计师。

sentences.en: She was intrigued.
sentences.zh: 她很感兴趣。

sentences.en: In part, it reminded her of home birth, which she experienced with her youngest child.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这让她想起了她生小儿子时的顺产经历。

sentences.en: Each seemed about reclaiming the most fundamental aspects of life, she said.
sentences.zh: 她说，这两者似乎都关乎找回生命中最基础的方面。

sentences.en: Caring for her mother in death would be an extension of what Suzanne did during the last years of her mother's life.
sentences.zh: 在母亲死后照顾她，将是苏珊娜在母亲生命的最后几年里所做事情的延续。

sentences.en: Her older brother, David, agreed.
sentences.zh: 她的哥哥大卫表示赞同。

sentences.en: So did her father, Conrad, a thoughtful man who favors plaid button-down shirts and keeps reading glasses perched on his almost bald head.
sentences.zh: 她的父亲康拉德也同意。他是一个沉思的人，喜欢穿格子衬衫，老花镜架在他几乎秃顶的头上。

sentences.en: A former priest, he had long been interested in Buddhism and open to creative rituals.
sentences.zh: 曾任神父的他长期对佛教感兴趣，并对创意的仪式持开放态度。

sentences.en: When he was a religious studies professor, his favorite class was
sentences.zh: 当他担任宗教研究教授时，他最喜欢的课是

sentences.en: The Inner Journey in Myth,
sentences.zh: 《神话、

sentences.en: Bible, and Literature, in which he had students keep personal journals and led them through guided imagery.
sentences.zh: 圣经和文学中的内心之旅》，在这门课上，他让学生写个人日志，并引导他们进行意象冥想。

sentences.en: It was a Friday afternoon in late February when Boucher arrived at Conrad and Susan's apartment with a bunch of flowers, her baskets, and a chest holding 25 pounds of dry ice.
sentences.zh: 那是2月下旬的一个周五下午，布歇带着一束花、她的篮子和一个装着25磅干冰的箱子来到了康拉德和苏珊的公寓。

sentences.en: David and Suzanne were in the living room with Conrad, along with Suzanne's two children,
sentences.zh: 大卫和苏珊娜与康拉德一起待在客厅里，还有苏珊娜的两个孩子，

sentences.en: Miles, 15, and Lila, 10.
sentences.zh: 15岁的米尔斯和10岁的莉拉。

sentences.en: Everyone was tired, but calm.
sentences.zh: 每个人都很疲惫，但很平静。

sentences.en: After Boucher sat down, they told her about the last day of Susan's life, how she was surrounded by the family, how they put their hands on her as she took her last breaths.
sentences.zh: 布歇坐下后，他们向她讲述了苏珊生命中的最后一天：她是如何被家人包围，在她咽下最后一口气时，他们是如何把手放在她身上的。

sentences.en: Then the adults took Boucher back to the bedroom, where Susan lay in her bed under a blanket that David bought for her, imprinted with four large photos of Susan, Conrad,
sentences.zh: 随后，成年人们带着布歇回到卧室，苏珊躺在床上，盖着一条大卫给她买的毯子，上面印有苏珊、康拉德、

sentences.en: their children, and grandchildren.
sentences.zh: 他们的孩子和孙辈的四张大照片。

sentences.en: Boucher approached her silently, touching one of her feet as a way to connect to her.
sentences.zh: 布歇默默地走近她，触摸她的脚作为与她连接的方式。

sentences.en: She asked everyone to gather washcloths and a couple of basins with warm water.
sentences.zh: 她请大家收集毛巾和几个装有温水的盆。

sentences.en: When Boucher wondered if Susan had a favorite scent,
sentences.zh: 当布歇想知道苏珊是否有最喜欢的香味时，

sentences.en: Suzanne mentioned rose, and Boucher added rose oil to the water.
sentences.zh: 苏珊娜提到了玫瑰，于是布歇将玫瑰精油加入水中。

sentences.en: Over the last year,
sentences.zh: 在过去的一年里，

sentences.en: Suzanne had regularly massaged her mother's face and temples with rose oil.
sentences.zh: 苏珊娜经常用玫瑰精油为母亲的面部和太阳穴按摩。

sentences.en: It had become an aroma of mother-daughter love.
sentences.zh: 这已经成为了母女之爱的芳香。

sentences.en: Then Boucher lit a candle and began to guide the family.
sentences.zh: 接着，布歇点燃了一根蜡烛，开始引导家属。

sentences.en: For the sake of ease, they cut off Susan's shirt.
sentences.zh: 为了方便起见，他们剪开了苏珊的衬衫。

sentences.en: Next,
sentences.zh: 接下来，

sentences.en: Boucher asked if everyone was okay if she pulled back the blanket, and as she did, she covered Susan's breasts and genitals with towels.
sentences.zh: 布歇询问大家拉开毯子是否可以，当她这么做时，她用毛巾盖住了苏珊的胸部和生殖器。

sentences.en: Conrad dipped a washcloth into the warm water and washed down along one side of his wife's body.
sentences.zh: 康拉德将一条毛巾浸入温水中，沿着妻子身体的一侧往下擦洗。

sentences.en: Suzanne, on the other side, put a washcloth to her face, along her neck, down her arm.
sentences.zh: 苏珊娜在另一侧，把毛巾敷在她的脸上、脖子上、手臂上。

sentences.en: All her life,
sentences.zh: 一生中，

sentences.en: Suzanne loved her mother's skin, the way it looked, the way it felt.
sentences.zh: 苏珊娜都深爱着母亲的皮肤，爱它的外观，爱它的触感。

sentences.en: Though she was grieving, touching and tending to her felt soothing.
sentences.zh: 尽管她在悲伤，但触摸和照料她让她感到安心。

sentences.en: They dipped and washed and dipped back into the warm water again before patting her skin dry.
sentences.zh: 他们蘸水、清洗，再次浸入温水中，然后把她的皮肤轻轻拍干。

sentences.en: In the months before his mother's death,
sentences.zh: 在母亲去世前的几个月里，

sentences.en: David was unsure what his role would be after she died.
sentences.zh: 大卫不确定自己在母亲去世后会扮演什么角色。

sentences.en: He knew only that he wanted to be in the room with his mother and to support his sister and father.
sentences.zh: 他只知道他想陪在母亲的房间里，支持他的姐姐和父亲。

sentences.en: He had taken care of his mother a couple of weeks a month, flying up from Los Angeles, where he works as an editor at ESPN.
sentences.zh: 他一个月会花几周时间照顾母亲，从他工作所在的洛杉矶飞过来，他在那里担任ESPN的编辑。

sentences.en: Toward the end of her life, he was with her nearly full time.
sentences.zh: 在她生命的最后阶段，他几乎全职陪在她身边。

sentences.en: Though his father, his sister, and home health aides had somewhat more physical intimacy with her body, he helped with most aspects of her care.
sentences.zh: 虽然他的父亲、姐姐和居家护理员对她身体的身体接触更多一些，但他参与了她护理的大部分方面。

sentences.en: As he stood at the bottom of the bed watching them wash her,
sentences.zh: 当他站在床尾看着他们为她清洗时，

sentences.en: David picked up his own cloth and began to press it along his mother's ankles and her feet.
sentences.zh: 大卫拿起自己的毛巾，开始在母亲的脚踝和脚上擦拭。

sentences.en: That evening in the bedroom,
sentences.zh: 那天傍晚在卧室里，

sentences.en: Suzanne and her daughter Lila looked through Susan's closet for her final outfit.
sentences.zh: 苏珊娜和她的女儿莉拉在苏珊的衣柜里为她寻找最后穿的衣服。

sentences.en: Lila picked a green button-up sweater and a pair of slacks that her grandmother liked.
sentences.zh: 莉拉挑了一件绿色的系扣毛衣和一条她奶奶喜欢的休闲裤。

sentences.en: Luce then showed Suzanne and Conrad how to gather the sleeves of the sweater and pull them up Susan's arms, as if dressing a small child.
sentences.zh: 露丝随后向苏珊娜和康拉德展示了如何聚拢毛衣的袖子，并把它们拉到苏珊的手臂上，就像给一个幼儿穿衣服一样。

sentences.en: It was easier now than it would be in several hours after rigor mortis set in, stiffening her muscles and joints for hours before they relaxed again.
sentences.zh: 现在做这事比几个小时后要容易，因为几个小时后尸僵就会开始，在肌肉和关节再次放松之前，它们会僵硬数小时。

sentences.en: And it was also easier than it had been in the last weeks, when Susan's pain often grew intense.
sentences.zh: 这也比过去几周要容易，当时苏珊的疼痛往往非常剧烈。

sentences.en: Could you imagine trying to do this two days ago?
sentences.zh: 你能想象两天前尝试做这个吗？

sentences.en: David said.
sentences.zh: 大卫说。

sentences.en: She would have pitched a fit.
sentences.zh: 她当时会大发脾气的。

sentences.en: David helped with her pants and slipped warm socks on his mother's feet.
sentences.zh: 大卫帮忙穿好裤子，并给母亲的脚套上了温暖的袜子。

sentences.en: Suzanne brushed her hair.
sentences.zh: 苏珊娜为她梳了头。

sentences.en: To prevent Susan's jaw from falling open, which happens as the muscles relax,
sentences.zh: 为了防止苏珊的下巴张开（肌肉放松时会发生这种情况），

sentences.en: Boucher and Suzanne placed her head on a pillow and tucked a rolled towel under her chin.
sentences.zh: 布歇和苏珊娜将她的头放在枕头上，并在她的下巴下塞了一条卷好的毛巾。

sentences.en: While the family took a break in the living room,
sentences.zh: 当家属在客厅休息时，

sentences.en: Boucher went to the balcony with her ice cheSt.
sentences.zh: 布歇带着她的冰柜去了阳台。

sentences.en: Using her hammer, she broke the dry ice into three-inch-thick chunks.
sentences.zh: 她用锤子把干冰砸成三英寸厚的块。

sentences.en: She wrapped each chunk in a piece of bed pad and placed the packets along Susan's body, from her armpits down to her hips.
sentences.zh: 她用床垫碎片把每一块干冰包起来，并将这些包裹沿着苏珊的身体从腋下一直放到臀部。

sentences.en: She put some on her stomach and a small one under her head.
sentences.zh: 她在她的胃上放了一些，在她的头下放了一个小的。

sentences.en: Suzanne still wasn't sure how long to keep her home.
sentences.zh: 苏珊娜仍然不确定要把她留在家中多久。

sentences.en: Though Boucher's clients typically choose three days for spiritual or religious reasons or because that's when they feel they'll be ready to part with the body,
sentences.zh: 尽管布歇的客户通常出于精神或宗教原因选择三天，或者因为那时他们觉得准备好与遗体告别了，

sentences.en: Suzanne thought that three days might be too woo-woo.
sentences.zh: 但苏珊娜觉得三天可能太迷信了。

sentences.en: Regardless, the ice, along with the open windows, would keep her body cool and slow down its decomposition.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，干冰加上开着的窗户，会让她的遗体保持凉爽并减缓腐烂。

sentences.en: Later that night,
sentences.zh: 那天深夜，

sentences.en: Suzanne headed home with her family while David slept in the guest room.
sentences.zh: 苏珊娜和家人回家了，而大卫睡在客房里。

sentences.en: Conrad got under a down comforter on a narrow wooden bed near Susan's where he had slept for weeks.
sentences.zh: 康拉德钻进了靠近苏珊的那张窄木床上的羽绒被里，他已经在那里睡了好几周。

sentences.en: He had designed the bed and built it with his son-in-law, Tony,
sentences.zh: 这张床是他设计并和女婿托尼一起制作的，

sentences.en: Suzanne's husband.
sentences.zh: 托尼是苏珊娜的丈夫。

sentences.en: It was just the height of Susan's hospital bed, allowing him to hold her hand at night.
sentences.zh: 它刚好和苏珊的病床同高，让他能在晚上握住她的手。

sentences.en: It was also narrow enough that he could tuck it away in the morning, leaving room for him, a hospice nurse, or a home health aide to care for Susan.
sentences.zh: 它也足够窄，以便他早上可以把它收起来，为他、临终关怀护士或居家护理员照顾苏珊留出空间。

sentences.en: When Conrad awoke the next morning, he went through his usual routine.
sentences.zh: 第二天早上康拉德醒来时，他重复了往常的例行公事。

sentences.en: He made coffee.
sentences.zh: 他煮了咖啡。

sentences.en: He looked at his favorite news websites.
sentences.zh: 他看着自己最喜欢的新闻网站。

sentences.en: He did it all quickly, anticipating that at any moment,
sentences.zh: 他动作飞快，心里预料着随时会有可能

sentences.en: Susan would call out to him.
sentences.zh: 苏珊会大声叫他。

sentences.en: She would need him for breakfast, for his companionship.
sentences.zh: 她吃早餐需要他，也需要他的陪伴。

sentences.en: Instead, that morning there was silence.
sentences.zh: 然而，那天早上却一片安静。

sentences.en: And then Conrad remembered she was gone.
sentences.zh: 随后康拉德想起来，她已经不在了。

sentences.en: In the United States, we have come to see death as an emergency.
sentences.zh: 在美国，我们渐渐将死亡视为一种紧急情况。

sentences.en: We call the doctors, the nurses, the police, the emergency workers, the funeral staff to take over for us.
sentences.zh: 我们打电话给医生、护士、警察、急救人员和殡仪馆员工，让他们接手一切。

sentences.en: They hurry corpses from hospital rooms or bedrooms into designated, chilled death spaces.
sentences.zh: 他们急忙把遗体从病房或卧室转移到指定的冷藏亡故空间。

sentences.en: They dig and fill the graves for us and drive our loved ones alone to the crematories.
sentences.zh: 他们为我们挖墓穴、填土，并开车把我们的亲人单独送到火葬场。

sentences.en: They turn on the furnace, lift the bodies,
sentences.zh: 他们开启火化炉，抬起遗体，

sentences.en: close the door.
sentences.zh: 关上炉门。

sentences.en: There may be no other rite of passage around which we have become more passive.
sentences.zh: 再也没有哪种人生仪轨能像这样让我们变得如此被动。

sentences.en: We carefully vet the doctors or midwives who will deliver our babies.
sentences.zh: 我们精心挑选将迎接我们宝宝出生的医生或助产士。

sentences.en: We pore over options for wedding venues and officiants.
sentences.zh: 我们仔细研究婚礼场地和主婚人的各种选择。

sentences.en: But often, we don't plan for death.
sentences.zh: 但通常，我们却不会为死亡做规划。

sentences.en: So when it arrives, we take what's easily available.
sentences.zh: 因此当死亡降临，我们只能接受那些唾手可得的安排。

sentences.en: In a 2016 survey by the National Funeral Directors Association,
sentences.zh: 根据全美殡仪馆长协会2016年的一项调查，

sentences.en: 81% of respondents said they called only one funeral home before making their decision.
sentences.zh: 81%的受访者表示他们在做出决定前只联系了一家殡仪馆。

sentences.en: If death practices reveal a culture's values, we choose convenience, outsourcing, an aversion to knowing and seeing too much.
sentences.zh: 如果说丧葬习俗折射出一个社会的价值观，那么我们选择的是便利、外包，以及对知晓和面对太多真相的排斥。

sentences.en: We used to live far closer to death.
sentences.zh: 过去，我们的生活与死亡要亲近得多。

sentences.en: If you died before the turn of the 20th century, women from your family and your community would lay you on a table or a bed.
sentences.zh: 如果你在20世纪之交前去世，你家族和社区里的女性会把你放在一张桌子或床上。

sentences.en: They would wash you,
sentences.zh: 她们会为你清洗身体，

sentences.en: dress you in simple clothes, comb your hair,
sentences.zh: 给你穿上朴素的衣服，梳理头发，

sentences.en: clip a lock of it to wear in a necklace.
sentences.zh: 剪下一缕头发做成项链随身佩戴。

sentences.en: As men dug your grave, family and friends would sit beside you, reciting prayers, singing, surrounding you with candles and flowers to help ward off the odor
sentences.zh: 当男人们为你挖墓穴时，家人和朋友会坐在你身旁，念诵祈祷文、唱歌，用蜡烛和鲜花把你团团围住，以驱散

sentences.en: from your decomposing corpse while the children came and went, unshielded from the inevitability of death and decay.
sentences.zh: 你那腐烂尸体散发的异味，而孩子们则在一旁进进出出，并未被刻意隔离，直面死亡与腐朽的不可避免。

sentences.en: And when it was time for your body to go, your family would wrap you in a shroud or a winding sheet, often made of wool or cashmere, and place you into a wood coffin,
sentences.zh: 当你的遗体该离去时，你的家人会用一块通常由羊毛或羊绒制成的寿布或裹尸布把你包裹起来，然后放进一口木棺里，

sentences.en: a six-sided burial box tapered at the feet and head.
sentences.zh: 那是一种头尾渐窄的六角形棺木。

sentences.en: The word casket, in contrast, is now used in the funeral industry to refer to a four-sided burial box.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，“casket”一词现在在殡葬业中用来指代四角棺木。

sentences.en: Finally, a group would carry your coffin on their shoulders to the backyard or the town cemetery and, after a small service, lower you into a newly dug hole in the ground.
sentences.zh: 最后，大家会把你的棺木扛在肩上送到后院或城镇公墓，举行一个小型的仪式后，将你缓缓放入刚挖好的墓穴中。

sentences.en: The whole process demanded work, attention, a reckoning.
sentences.zh: 整个过程需要付出劳力、倾注心力，还要面对现实。

sentences.en: That began to change during the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 这种情况在南北战争期间开始发生改变。

sentences.en: For the first time in the United States, men died en masse, far from family.
sentences.zh: 在美国历史上，人们第一次大规模地客死异乡、远离家人。

sentences.en: Families who could afford to shipped the bodies back home.
sentences.zh: 那些负担得起费用的家庭会将遗体运回老家。

sentences.en: But the train trips were long.
sentences.zh: 但火车旅程漫长。

sentences.en: Some railways began to refuse decomposing bodies in wood coffins, and families wanted their sons, brothers, and husbands looking as preserved as possible, as Drew Gilpin Faust
sentences.zh: 正如德鲁·吉尔平·福斯特在

sentences.en: recounts in
sentences.zh: 《这受难的共和国：

sentences.en: This Republic of Suffering,
sentences.zh: 死亡与美国内战》

sentences.en: Death, and the American Civil War.
sentences.zh: 一书中所述，一些铁路公司开始拒绝运送装在木棺里的腐烂遗体，而家属们则希望他们的儿子、兄弟和丈夫能尽可能地保持完好。

sentences.en: Surgeons, undertakers, and others began performing rudimentary embalming of soldiers using arsenic, zinc chloride, or other ingredients.
sentences.zh: 外科医生、殡葬从业者和其他人员开始使用砷、氯化锌或其他成分对士兵进行最初级的防腐处理。

sentences.en: It was President
sentences.zh: 不过，正是总统

sentences.en: Abraham Lincoln's death, though, that introduced embalming to the general public.
sentences.zh: 亚伯拉罕·林肯的去世，才将防腐技术引入大众视野。

sentences.en: His embalmed body was on display in Washington for nearly a week and then traveled by train for two more weeks, making frequent stops for viewings, ending up in Springfield,
sentences.zh: 他的防腐遗体在华盛顿展出了近一周，随后又坐了两周的火车，途中频繁停靠供人瞻仰，最终运抵伊利诺伊州

sentences.en: Illinois.
sentences.zh: 斯普林菲尔德。

sentences.en: Initially, observers noted that his face was remarkably lifelike.
sentences.zh: 起初，观察人士注意到他的面容宛如生前一般栩栩如生。

sentences.en: A few days in, as one New York editor wrote,
sentences.zh: 几天后，正如一位纽约编辑所写，

sentences.en: Lincoln, who was re-embalmed multiple times during the journey, was a ghastly shadow.
sentences.zh: 在途中被多次重新防腐的林肯，已经成了一个面目可怖的阴影。

sentences.en: The funeral industry emerged over the following decades, faster in urban areas than in rural ones.
sentences.zh: 在随后的几十年里，殡葬业兴起，城市地区的发展速度快于农村地区。

sentences.en: In 1890, there were 9,891 funeral directors in the United States.
sentences.zh: 1890年，美国有9,891名殡仪馆长。

sentences.en: Thirty years later, the figure had more than doubled, despite the fact that the death rate had dropped substantially, as Gary Latterman, a professor of religion
sentences.zh: 三十年后，这一数字翻了一倍多，尽管死亡率已经大幅下降，正如埃默里大学宗教学教授

sentences.en: at Emory University, writes in
sentences.zh: 加里·拉特曼在

sentences.en: Rest in Peace, a cultural history of death and funeral homes in 20th century America.
sentences.zh: 《安息吧：20世纪美国死亡与殡仪馆的文化史》一书中所写的那样。

sentences.en: By the 1930s, with increasing numbers of people dying in hospitals instead of homes, death became professionalized.
sentences.zh: 到了20世纪30年代，随着越来越多的人在医院而不是家中去世，死亡实现了专业化。

sentences.en: Funeral industry groups had lobbied state legislatures to create laws about who could prepare and bury bodies.
sentences.zh: 殡葬行业组织向州议会游说，通过了关于谁有资格处理和埋葬遗体的法律。

sentences.en: And embalmed bodies, which funeral directors promoted as sanitary, medical, and therefore necessary, became the centerpieces of funerals.
sentences.zh: 而被殡仪馆长标榜为卫生、医疗且因此必不可少的防腐遗体，成为了葬礼的核心。

sentences.en: Funeral directors, not families, became the new death experts.
sentences.zh: 殡仪馆长而非家属，成了新的死亡专家。

sentences.en: Embalming was performed on a majority of corpses by the middle of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 到20世纪中叶，大多数遗体都要接受防腐处理。

sentences.en: Now, experts estimate, about 50% of dead bodies in the United States are embalmed.
sentences.zh: 现在，专家估计美国大约50%的逝者遗体都经过防腐处理。

sentences.en: The funeral industry doesn't publish statistics.
sentences.zh: 殡葬行业并不公开统计数据。

sentences.en: During a roughly three-hour process, the embalmer washes the body with a disinfectant solution and massages and moves the limbs to loosen the stiffness from rigor mortis.
sentences.zh: 在大约三个小时的程序中，防腐师用消毒液清洗遗体，并按摩和活动四肢以缓解死后僵硬。

sentences.en: He, most funeral directors are men, though the number of women is rising, sets the facial features.
sentences.zh: 他（大多数殡仪馆长都是男性，尽管女性人数正在增加）会调整面部特征。

sentences.en: He closes the eyelids, sometimes using adhesive glue or a plastic eye cap, and the mouth, suturing or sewing the jaw to the guMs.
sentences.zh: 他会闭上眼睑（有时会使用医用胶水或塑料眼罩），并通过缝合或将下颌缝到牙龈上来合上嘴巴。

sentences.en: Next, he cuts into the base of the throat near the clavicle to reach a carotid artery and inserts a small tube through which a machine that looks like an oversized blender
sentences.zh: 接着，他在锁骨附近的喉咙底部切开一个切口以找到颈动脉，并插入一根小软管，通过一台看起来像超大号搅拌机的机器

sentences.en: pumps several gallons of embalming fluid into the body.
sentences.zh: 将几加仑防腐液泵入体内。

sentences.en: The fluid, a tinted potion of formaldehyde and other chemicals, some funeral homes now offer a non-formaldehyde alternative, is designed to erase the natural pallor of death
sentences.zh: 这种液体是甲醛和其他化学物质的带色混合物（现在一些殡仪馆提供不含甲醛的替代品），旨在抹去死亡带来的天然苍白

sentences.en: and plump up the skin.
sentences.zh: 并让皮肤丰盈起来。

sentences.en: From a nearby vein, he is meanwhile draining the blood.
sentences.zh: 同时，他从附近的静脉中将血液排出。

sentences.en: Finally, before fixing the hair, applying cosmetics, and dressing the body in clothes chosen by family members or friends, he makes one more incision, this one
sentences.zh: 最后，在整理头发、涂抹化妆品并给遗体穿上家属或朋友挑选的衣服之前，他还要再做一个切口，位置在

sentences.en: in the lower abdomen.
sentences.zh: 下腹部。

sentences.en: He inserts a tube attached to a trocar, a long, sharp surgical instrument to puncture the intestines, the stomach, the lungs, and the bladder and suction out fluids and gases,
sentences.zh: 他插入一根连接着套管针（一种用于刺穿肠道、胃、肺和膀胱的长而锋利的手术器械）的管子，抽吸出体液和气体，

sentences.en: replacing them with a stronger mix of embalming fluids.
sentences.zh: 然后注入浓度更高的防腐液混合物。

sentences.en: When Jessica Mitford wrote her 1963 best-selling investigation into the funeral industry, the American way of death, she was particularly critical of embalming and claimed
sentences.zh: 当杰西卡·米特福德在1963年写下她那本关于殡葬业的畅销调查著作《美国人的死亡方式》时，她对防腐技术进行了严厉批评，并声称

sentences.en: that funeral directors were little more than swindlers, peddling products and services that people didn't need and couldn't afford.
sentences.zh: 殡仪馆长不过是诈骗犯，兜售人们不需要也买不起的产品和235服务。

sentences.en: More than a decade later, the Federal Trade Commission held public hearings on opaque pricing and other funeral industry problems, with thousands of comments
sentences.zh: 十多年后，联邦贸易委员会就定价不透明和其他殡葬行业问题举行了听证会，

sentences.en: submitted by a frustrated and angry public.
sentences.zh: 沮丧和愤怒的公众提交了数千条意见。

sentences.en: It wasn't until 1984, over the objections of the funeral industry, that the FTC created the Funeral Rule, which, among other things, requires funeral directors
sentences.zh: 直到1984年，在殡葬行业的反对声中，联邦贸易委员会才制定了《殡葬规则》，其中一项规定要求殡仪馆长

sentences.en: to give prices by phone and disclose that, aside from special exceptions in some states, embalming is not required by law.
sentences.zh: 必须通过电话提供价格信息，并披露除某些州的特殊例外情况外，法律并不强制要求进行防腐处理。

sentences.en: Though the industry has improved from Mitford's days, many funeral homes still promote embalming.
sentences.zh: 尽管该行业自米特福德的时代以来有所改善，但许多殡仪馆仍然大力推销防腐服务。

sentences.en: They say it's the choice that brings you peace of mind and preserves the body.
sentences.zh: 他们说这能让你安心并保存遗体。

sentences.en: It delays, but doesn't stop, decomposition, while creating the best possible appearance.
sentences.zh: 它能延缓而非阻止腐烂，同时呈现出尽可能好的外观。

sentences.en: One funeral arranger told me she was trained at a large Los Angeles funeral home to tell customers that not embalming was illegal because of the danger to you and the danger
sentences.zh: 一位殡葬统筹师告诉我，她在洛杉矶一家大型殡仪馆受训时，被教导要告诉客户，不做防腐处理是违法的，因为会对你和

sentences.en: to your family.
sentences.zh: 你的家人构成危险。

sentences.en: In reality, a vast majority of people die of non-communicable diseases, and in general, people are more contagious alive than dead.
sentences.zh: 现实中，绝大多数人死于非传染性疾病，而且一般来说，活人比死人更具传染性。

sentences.en: A symbiotic relationship has developed between our cultural assumptions about what constitutes the right funeral and the funeral industry's interests, notes Tanya Marsh,
sentences.zh: 专攻殡葬和墓园法的维克森林大学法学院教授

sentences.en: a professor at
sentences.zh: 坦娅·马什

sentences.en: Wake Forest University
sentences.zh: 指出，

sentences.en: School of Law who specializes in funeral and cemetery law.
sentences.zh: 在我们关于什么才是一场“正确”葬礼的文化假设与殡葬行业的利益之间，已经形成了一种共生关系。

sentences.en: We were complicit in handing over control of this sphere of life to a profit-making industry.
sentences.zh: 我们同流合污，将生活这一领域的控制权拱手交给了以盈利为目的的行业。

sentences.en: If we don't like it, we can take it back.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不喜欢这样，我们可以把它夺回来。

sentences.en: In some religions and cultures, community members do take control by tending to corpses themselves.
sentences.zh: 在某些宗教和文化中，社区成员确实通过亲自照料遗体来掌握主动权。
